name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun, with no atmosphere to retain heat.

name: Venus
description: The hottest planet in the solar system due to a runaway greenhouse atmosphere of carbon dioxide.

name: Earth
description: The only known planet with liquid water oceans covering most of its surface.

name: Mars
description: Known as the Red Planet for its iron-oxide-rich surface dust.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet in the solar system, a gas giant with a Great Red Spot storm.

name: Saturn
description: Famous for its spectacular ring system made mostly of ice particles.

name: Uranus
description: An ice giant that rotates almost on its side, likely from a past massive collision.

name: Neptune
description: The windiest planet in the solar system, with storms reaching supersonic speeds.

name: Pluto
description: Reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, it has a heart-shaped nitrogen-ice glacier.

name: Ceres
description: The largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet located there.

name: Eris
description: A distant, icy dwarf planet whose discovery helped trigger Pluto's reclassification.

name: Haumea
description: An oddly elongated dwarf planet that spins so fast it is shaped like a football, and has a thin ring.

name: Makemake
description: A reddish, icy dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt named after a Rapa Nui creation deity.

name: Moon
description: Earth's only natural satellite, thought to have formed from debris after a giant impact.

name: Io
description: The most volcanically active body in the solar system, driven by tidal heating from Jupiter.

name: Europa
description: An icy moon of Jupiter believed to hide a subsurface ocean beneath its frozen crust.

name: Ganymede
description: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than the planet Mercury.

name: Callisto
description: One of the most heavily cratered bodies in the solar system, largely unchanged for billions of years.

name: Titan
description: Saturn's largest moon, with thick clouds and lakes of liquid methane on its surface.

name: Enceladus
description: A small icy moon that sprays plumes of water vapor from its south pole.

name: Triton
description: Neptune's largest moon, notable for orbiting backwards relative to the planet's rotation.

name: Titania
description: The largest moon of Uranus, marked by canyons far deeper than the Grand Canyon.

name: Oberon
description: The outermost major moon of Uranus, heavily cratered with a reddish surface.

name: Rhea
description: Saturn's second-largest moon, composed mostly of water ice.

name: Iapetus
description: Known for its striking two-tone coloring, one hemisphere dark and one bright.

name: Phobos
description: The larger of Mars's two moons, orbiting so close and fast it rises twice a day.

name: Deimos
description: The smaller, outer moon of Mars, likely a captured asteroid.

name: Mimas
description: A small moon of Saturn with a giant crater that gives it a Death Star-like appearance.

name: Dione
description: An icy moon of Saturn with bright, wispy cliffs of fractured ice.

name: Tethys
description: A Saturnian moon almost entirely composed of water ice, with a massive canyon system.

name: Miranda
description: The smallest of Uranus's major moons, with an extraordinarily varied, jumbled terrain.

name: Ariel
description: The brightest of Uranus's major moons, with a surface of ice canyons and lava-like flows.

name: Umbriel
description: The darkest of Uranus's major moons, heavily cratered and ancient.

name: Charon
description: Pluto's largest moon, so massive relative to Pluto that the two form a binary system.

name: Vesta
description: One of the largest bodies in the asteroid belt, bright enough to sometimes be seen with the naked eye.

name: Bennu
description: A carbon-rich near-Earth asteroid sampled by NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission.

name: Ryugu
description: A diamond-shaped near-Earth asteroid visited and sampled by Japan's Hayabusa2 mission.

name: Apophis
description: A near-Earth asteroid that will pass closer to Earth than some satellites in 2029.

name: Eros
description: An elongated near-Earth asteroid, the first ever to be orbited and landed on by a spacecraft.

name: Itokawa
description: A small, peanut-shaped near-Earth asteroid, the first to have samples returned to Earth.

name: Psyche
description: A metal-rich asteroid thought to be the exposed core of an early planetary building block.

name: Ida
description: An asteroid in the main belt that was found to have its own tiny moon, Dactyl.

name: Halley's Comet
description: The most famous periodic comet, visible from Earth roughly every 76 years.

name: Hale-Bopp
description: One of the brightest comets of the 20th century, visible to the naked eye for a record 18 months.

name: Sun
description: The star at the center of the solar system, a yellow dwarf that makes up 99.8% of the system's mass.

name: Sirius
description: The brightest star in Earth's night sky, a blue-white star twice the mass of the Sun.

name: Proxima Centauri
description: The closest known star to the Sun, a small red dwarf orbited by at least one Earth-sized planet.

name: Vega
description: One of the brightest stars in the northern sky, and was the northern pole star around 12,000 BCE.

name: Betelgeuse
description: A red supergiant so vast that, if it replaced the Sun, its surface would extend past Jupiter's orbit.

name: Sagittarius A*
description: The supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, about 4 million times the Sun's mass.

name: M87*
description: A supermassive black hole in galaxy M87, the first black hole ever directly photographed, in 2019.

name: Cygnus X-1
description: One of the first black holes ever identified, formed from the collapse of a massive star.

name: Orion Nebula
description: A vast stellar nursery visible to the naked eye, where thousands of new stars are being born.

name: Crab Nebula
description: The expanding remnant of a supernova recorded by astronomers in the year 1054.

name: Ring Nebula
description: A glowing shell of gas cast off by a dying star, forming a famous ring shape as seen from Earth.

name: Milky Way
description: The barred spiral galaxy containing the solar system, home to at least 100 billion stars.

name: Andromeda Galaxy
description: The nearest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, on a slow collision course with it.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
description: A classic spiral galaxy famous for its clearly defined arms, seen interacting with a smaller companion galaxy.

name: TON 618
description: One of the most massive black holes ever found, powering a hyperluminous quasar.

name: OJ 287
description: A binary black hole system whose smaller companion punches through the larger one's disk every ~12 years, causing predictable flares.

name: GRO J1655-40
description: A stellar-mass black hole in a binary system, notable for jets that appeared to move faster than light (an illusion of perspective).

name: V404 Cygni
description: A black hole binary that erupted dramatically in 2015 after 26 years of quiet, briefly becoming one of the brightest X-ray sources in the sky.

name: 3C 273
description: The first quasar ever identified and one of the most luminous objects in the observable universe.

name: 3C 48
description: One of the earliest known quasars, first cataloged as a mysterious radio source before its true nature was understood.

name: ULAS J1120+0641
description: One of the most distant known quasars, seen as it was less than a billion years after the Big Bang.

name: APM 08279+5255
description: An extremely luminous, gravitationally lensed quasar surrounded by a massive reservoir of water vapor.

name: Markarian 231
description: The closest known quasar to Earth, harboring a binary supermassive black hole at its core.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
description: The third-largest galaxy in the Local Group, a spiral galaxy visible to the naked eye under dark skies.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
description: A galaxy with a bright nucleus, large central bulge, and a prominent dust lane, resembling a wide-brimmed hat.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud
description: A satellite galaxy of the Milky Way visible to the naked eye from the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Centaurus A
description: A giant elliptical galaxy with an active supermassive black hole launching a jet of particles thousands of light-years long.

name: Eagle Nebula
description: Home to the Pillars of Creation, towering columns of gas and dust where new stars are forming.

name: Helix Nebula
description: One of the closest planetary nebulae to Earth, nicknamed the 'Eye of God' for its ring-like appearance.

name: Cat's Eye Nebula
description: A planetary nebula with an intricate, layered structure suggesting repeated bursts of material from its dying central star.

name: Nereid
description: One of the most eccentric orbits of any moon in the solar system, swinging from close to Neptune to far beyond it.

name: Hyperion
description: An irregularly shaped, sponge-like moon of Saturn that tumbles chaotically rather than rotating predictably.

name: Amalthea
description: A small, reddish inner moon of Jupiter, likely stained by sulfur particles from Io's volcanic eruptions.

name: 2 Pallas
description: The third-largest object in the asteroid belt, tilted at a steep angle unlike most other large asteroids.

name: 3 Juno
description: One of the first asteroids discovered, bright enough to occasionally be visible with the naked eye.

name: 2060 Chiron
description: A centaur that orbits between Saturn and Uranus, classified as both an asteroid and a comet due to its occasional cometary activity.

name: C/2020 F3 (NEOWISE)
description: A long-period comet that became the brightest seen from the Northern Hemisphere in over two decades when it passed by in 2020.

name: Rigel
description: A blue supergiant and the brightest star in the constellation Orion, tens of thousands of times more luminous than the Sun.

name: Antares
description: A red supergiant so large that, like Betelgeuse, it could engulf the orbit of Mars if placed at the center of the solar system.

name: Polaris
description: The current North Star, closely aligned with Earth's axis of rotation, making it appear nearly fixed in the sky.

name: Alpha Centauri A
description: The brighter member of the nearest star system to the Sun, a yellow star very similar in size and temperature to our own.

name: Orion
description: One of the most recognizable constellations, depicting a hunter flanked by two dogs, with a distinctive three-star belt.

name: Ursa Major
description: The third-largest constellation, home to the Big Dipper asterism used for centuries to find true north.

name: Ursa Minor
description: Contains Polaris, the North Star, at the tip of its tail, making it a key reference for celestial navigation.

name: Cassiopeia
description: Named for a vain queen in Greek mythology, easily spotted by its distinctive W or M shape of five bright stars.

name: Leo
description: A zodiac constellation resembling a crouching lion, with a curved 'sickle' of stars marking its head and mane.

name: Scorpius
description: A zodiac constellation whose curving tail of stars traces the shape of a scorpion across the southern summer sky.

name: Crux
description: The smallest of all 88 official constellations, known as the Southern Cross and featured on several national flags.

name: Cygnus
description: Depicts a swan flying along the Milky Way, its brightest stars forming the well-known Northern Cross asterism.

name: Andromeda (constellation)
description: Named for a mythological princess, this constellation is best known as the location of the Andromeda Galaxy.

name: Sagittarius (constellation)
description: A zodiac constellation shaped like a teapot, pointing toward the center of the Milky Way galaxy.

name: Proxima Centauri b
description: The closest known exoplanet to Earth, orbiting within the habitable zone of the nearest star to the Sun.

name: TRAPPIST-1e
description: Considered the most Earth-like of the seven rocky planets in the TRAPPIST-1 system, likely capable of retaining liquid water.

name: Kepler-452b
description: Nicknamed 'Earth's cousin,' orbiting a Sun-like star at a similar distance and period as Earth around the Sun.

name: 51 Pegasi b
description: The first exoplanet discovered orbiting a Sun-like star, a 'hot Jupiter' whose discovery launched modern exoplanet science.

name: HD 209458 b
description: Nicknamed 'Osiris,' the first exoplanet observed transiting its star and the first found to have an atmosphere.

name: Kepler-16b
description: A 'circumbinary' planet orbiting two stars at once, evoking Tatooine's twin sunsets from Star Wars.

name: WASP-12b
description: An extreme hot Jupiter orbiting so close to its star that it is slowly being torn apart and consumed.

name: 55 Cancri e
description: A scorching lava world completing an orbit in under 18 hours, theorized to have a carbon-rich interior.

name: Antlia
description: A faint southern constellation representing an air pump, one of the constellations introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 18th century.

name: Apus
description: A small southern constellation representing a bird-of-paradise, first depicted on a 16th-century celestial globe.

name: Aquarius
description: A zodiac constellation depicting a water-bearer, home to the radiant point of the annual Aquariid meteor showers.

name: Aquila
description: Represents an eagle in Greek mythology, marked by its brightest star Altair, one point of the Summer Triangle.

name: Ara
description: A southern constellation representing an altar, located near the tail of Scorpius.

name: Aries
description: A zodiac constellation depicting a ram, historically marking the location of the vernal equinox in ancient astronomy.

name: Auriga
description: Represents a charioteer, marked by the bright star Capella and several notable open star clusters.

name: Boötes
description: Represents a herdsman, home to Arcturus, one of the brightest stars in the night sky.

name: Caelum
description: One of the faintest constellations, representing an engraving tool, introduced by Lacaille.

name: Camelopardalis
description: A large but faint northern constellation representing a giraffe.

name: Cancer
description: The dimmest zodiac constellation, representing a crab, home to the Beehive Cluster.

name: Canes Venatici
description: Represents hunting dogs, home to the Whirlpool Galaxy.

name: Canis Major
description: Represents the greater dog, containing Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky.

name: Canis Minor
description: Represents the lesser dog, marked by the bright star Procyon.

name: Capricornus
description: A zodiac constellation depicting a sea-goat, one of the faintest zodiac constellations.

name: Carina
description: Represents the keel of the ship Argo, home to the bright star Canopus and the Carina Nebula.

name: Centaurus
description: Represents a centaur, home to Alpha Centauri, the closest star system to the Sun.

name: Cepheus
description: Represents a mythological king of Aethiopia, home to several notable variable stars.

name: Cetus
description: Represents a sea monster or whale, home to the famous variable star Mira.

name: Chamaeleon
description: A small, faint southern constellation representing a chameleon.

name: Circinus
description: One of the smallest constellations, representing a drafting compass.

name: Columba
description: Represents a dove, sometimes associated with the dove released from Noah's Ark.

name: Coma Berenices
description: Named after the hair of Queen Berenice II of Egypt, home to a rich cluster of galaxies.

name: Corona Australis
description: Represents a southern crown, one of the 48 constellations listed by the ancient astronomer Ptolemy.

name: Corona Borealis
description: Represents a northern crown, associated in Greek mythology with the crown of Ariadne.

name: Corvus
description: Represents a crow, a small constellation associated with the myth of Apollo.

name: Crater
description: Represents a cup, associated in mythology with the god Apollo.

name: Delphinus
description: A small constellation representing a dolphin, easily recognized despite containing no especially bright stars.

name: Dorado
description: Represents a dolphinfish, home to most of the Large Magellanic Cloud.

name: Draco
description: Represents a dragon coiled around the north celestial pole, one of the largest constellations.

name: Equuleus
description: The second-smallest constellation, representing a small horse or foal.

name: Eridanus
description: Represents a river, one of the largest constellations, stretching from near Orion to the southern star Achernar.

name: Fornax
description: Represents a furnace, introduced by Lacaille and home to the Fornax Cluster of galaxies.

name: Gemini
description: A zodiac constellation representing twins, marked by the bright stars Castor and Pollux.

name: Grus
description: Represents a crane, one of twelve constellations introduced by Dutch navigators in the late 16th century.

name: Hercules
description: Represents the mythological hero, home to the Great Globular Cluster, one of the brightest globular clusters visible from the north.

name: Horologium
description: Represents a pendulum clock, one of the faintest constellations introduced by Lacaille.

name: Hydra
description: The largest of all 88 constellations, representing a water serpent.

name: Hydrus
description: Represents a male water snake, not to be confused with the much larger constellation Hydra.

name: Indus
description: Represents an indigenous person, one of twelve constellations introduced by Dutch navigators.

name: Lacerta
description: A small, faint northern constellation representing a lizard.

name: Leo Minor
description: A faint constellation representing a smaller lion, introduced in the 17th century.

name: Lepus
description: Represents a hare, positioned just south of Orion.

name: Libra
description: The only zodiac constellation representing an inanimate object, a set of scales.

name: Lupus
description: Represents a wolf, one of the 48 constellations listed by Ptolemy in antiquity.

name: Lynx
description: A faint northern constellation representing a lynx, said to require lynx-like eyesight to see.

name: Lyra
description: Represents a lyre, home to Vega, one of the brightest stars in the northern sky.

name: Mensa
description: The faintest of all 88 constellations, named after Table Mountain in South Africa.

name: Microscopium
description: Represents a microscope, one of the faint constellations introduced by Lacaille.

name: Monoceros
description: Represents a unicorn, a faint constellation straddling the celestial equator near Orion.

name: Musca
description: Represents a fly, the only official constellation depicting an insect.

name: Norma
description: Represents a carpenter's square, one of the smaller constellations introduced by Lacaille.

name: Octans
description: Contains the south celestial pole, though it has no bright star marking it precisely as Polaris does in the north.

name: Ophiuchus
description: Represents a serpent-bearer, straddling the ecliptic and sometimes called the 13th zodiac sign.

name: Pavo
description: Represents a peacock, one of twelve constellations introduced by Dutch navigators.

name: Pegasus
description: Represents a winged horse from Greek mythology, marked by the Great Square asterism.

name: Perseus
description: Represents the mythological hero, home to the annual Perseid meteor shower's radiant point.

name: Phoenix
description: Represents the mythical bird reborn from ashes, one of twelve constellations introduced by Dutch navigators.

name: Pictor
description: Represents a painter's easel, a faint constellation introduced by Lacaille.

name: Pisces
description: A zodiac constellation representing two fish, containing the vernal equinox point in modern astronomy.

name: Piscis Austrinus
description: Represents a southern fish, home to the bright star Fomalhaut.

name: Puppis
description: Represents the stern of the ship Argo, the largest of the three constellations formed from the ancient constellation Argo Navis.

name: Pyxis
description: Represents a mariner's compass, a small constellation once considered part of the ship Argo Navis.

name: Reticulum
description: A small southern constellation representing a reticle, the crosshairs used in optical instruments.

name: Sagitta
description: Represents an arrow, the third-smallest constellation despite being one of the oldest recognized.

name: Sculptor
description: Represents a sculptor's workshop, home to the south galactic pole.

name: Scutum
description: Represents a shield, home to a dense field of the Milky Way including the Wild Duck Cluster.

name: Serpens
description: The only constellation split into two separate regions, representing a serpent held by Ophiuchus.

name: Sextans
description: Represents an astronomical sextant, a faint constellation introduced by Johannes Hevelius.

name: Taurus
description: A zodiac constellation representing a bull, home to both the Pleiades and Hyades star clusters.

name: Telescopium
description: Represents a telescope, one of the fainter constellations introduced by Lacaille.

name: Triangulum (constellation)
description: A small northern constellation representing a triangle, home to the Triangulum Galaxy.

name: Triangulum Australe
description: Represents a southern triangle, one of twelve constellations introduced by Dutch navigators.

name: Tucana
description: Represents a toucan, home to the Small Magellanic Cloud and the bright globular cluster 47 Tucanae.

name: Vela
description: Represents the sails of the ship Argo, part of the ancient constellation Argo Navis.

name: Virgo
description: The largest zodiac constellation, home to the Virgo Cluster of thousands of galaxies.

name: Volans
description: Represents a flying fish, one of twelve constellations introduced by Dutch navigators.

name: Vulpecula
description: Represents a small fox, home to the Dumbbell Nebula, one of the first planetary nebulae discovered.

name: Himalia
description: The largest of Jupiter's irregular moons, likely a captured asteroid orbiting far beyond the main Galilean moons.

name: Janus
description: Shares nearly the same orbit as the moon Epimetheus, the two swapping positions every four years without colliding.

name: Epimetheus
description: Co-orbital with Janus in one of the most unusual orbital relationships in the solar system.

name: Pan
description: A tiny, walnut-shaped moon that orbits within a gap in Saturn's rings, sweeping the gap clear of debris.

name: Puck
description: The largest of Uranus's inner moons, named after the mischievous sprite from Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

name: Proteus
description: One of the darkest objects in the solar system, so close to Neptune that it is difficult to observe from Earth.

name: Larissa
description: An irregularly shaped inner moon of Neptune, discovered during a stellar occultation before being confirmed by Voyager 2.

name: Nix
description: One of Pluto's small outer moons, tumbling chaotically due to the complex gravity of the Pluto-Charon binary system.

name: Hydra
description: The outermost of Pluto's known moons, named after the many-headed serpent of Greek mythology.

name: 10 Hygiea
description: The fourth-largest object in the asteroid belt, round enough that it has been considered for dwarf planet status.

name: 704 Interamnia
description: One of the largest main-belt asteroids not yet visited by any spacecraft, named after the Latin name for Teramo, Italy.

name: 15 Eunomia
description: The largest asteroid of the stony S-type, and the most massive asteroid without a spacecraft visit as of its discovery era.

name: 511 Davida
description: One of the largest main-belt asteroids, irregularly shaped and dark in color.

name: 21 Lutetia
description: A heavily cratered metallic asteroid visited by the Rosetta spacecraft on its way to comet 67P.

name: Comet Encke
description: Has the shortest orbital period of any known comet, returning past the Sun once every 3.3 years.

name: Comet Swift-Tuttle
description: The parent body of the annual Perseid meteor shower, with a nucleus larger than the object believed to have ended the dinosaurs.

name: Comet Hyakutake
description: Passed unusually close to Earth in 1996, appearing as one of the brightest comets in decades with an exceptionally long visible tail.

name: Deneb
description: One of the most luminous stars known, a blue-white supergiant marking the tail of the constellation Cygnus.

name: Capella
description: Actually a system of four stars appearing as one bright point, the brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

name: Arcturus
description: The brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, an aging orange giant nearing the end of its life.

name: Aldebaran
description: A red giant marking the eye of the bull in Taurus, though it only appears aligned with the more distant Hyades cluster.

name: Spica
description: A close binary of hot blue giant stars so near each other that their mutual gravity distorts them into egg shapes.

name: Fomalhaut
description: Surrounded by a debris disk that once hosted a directly imaged exoplanet candidate, since found likely to be a dust cloud.

name: Altair
description: Spins so rapidly that it is flattened into an oblate shape, completing a full rotation in under 9 hours.

name: Achernar
description: One of the least spherical stars known, flattened by extremely fast rotation into a shape wider at its equator than its poles.

name: A0620-00
description: One of the closest known stellar-mass black holes to Earth, discovered via an X-ray nova outburst in 1975.

name: GRS 1915+105
description: One of the most massive stellar black holes known in our galaxy, famous for launching relativistic jets nicknamed a 'microquasar.'

name: NGC 4889 Black Hole
description: One of the most massive black holes ever measured, sitting at the center of a giant elliptical galaxy in the Coma Cluster.

name: Phoenix A
description: An extraordinarily massive black hole at the heart of the Phoenix Cluster, forming stars at a rate unusual for its host galaxy type.

name: 3C 279
description: A highly variable blazar whose brightness can change dramatically within days, among the most studied quasars in the sky.

name: PDS 456
description: One of the most luminous quasars in the nearby universe, driving powerful winds that blow gas out of its host galaxy.

name: J0313-1806
description: One of the most distant quasars ever found, observed as it existed when the universe was less than 700 million years old.

name: PKS 2126-158
description: One of the most luminous quasars known, radiating energy equivalent to trillions of Suns.

name: Bode's Galaxy
description: A grand-design spiral galaxy with well-defined arms, a favorite target for amateur astronomers due to its brightness.

name: Cigar Galaxy
description: A starburst galaxy producing new stars at a rate ten times faster than the Milky Way, likely triggered by a close pass with its neighbor.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy
description: A large, face-on spiral galaxy with asymmetric arms shaped by gravitational interactions with several companion galaxies.

name: Cartwheel Galaxy
description: Its distinctive ring shape was formed by a smaller galaxy passing directly through its center, triggering a ripple of star formation.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud
description: A dwarf galaxy visible to the naked eye from the Southern Hemisphere, gravitationally linked to its larger neighbor, the LMC.

name: Lagoon Nebula
description: A vast stellar nursery visible to the naked eye, containing a young star cluster embedded within its glowing gas.

name: Trifid Nebula
description: Named for the dark dust lanes that appear to split its glowing gas into three lobes.

name: Rosette Nebula
description: A rose-shaped ring of glowing gas surrounding a young cluster of stars whose radiation carved out its central cavity.

name: Tarantula Nebula
description: The most active star-forming region known in the nearby universe, located within the Large Magellanic Cloud.

name: Veil Nebula
description: The delicate, glowing remains of a massive star that exploded as a supernova roughly 10,000 years ago.

name: Kepler-186f
description: The first Earth-sized planet found within the habitable zone of another star, orbiting a cool red dwarf.

name: GJ 1214 b
description: A 'mini-Neptune' thought to be a water world, with a thick steamy atmosphere shrouding its surface.

name: HR 8799 b
description: One of the first exoplanets ever directly photographed, part of a system with four giant planets imaged in orbit around their star.

name: Gliese 667 Cc
description: Orbits within the habitable zone of one star in a triple-star system, one of the most Earth-like exoplanets known at its discovery.

name: TOI-700 d
description: The first Earth-sized habitable-zone planet discovered by NASA's TESS mission.

name: Canopus
description: The second-brightest star in the night sky, a yellow-white supergiant used for spacecraft navigation.

name: Procyon
description: A nearby yellow-white subgiant, one of the closest bright stars to the Sun.

name: Acrux
description: The brightest star of the Southern Cross and the southernmost first-magnitude star.

name: Pollux
description: An orange giant and the closest giant star to the Sun, host to a confirmed exoplanet.

name: Regulus
description: A rapidly spinning blue-white star flattened into an oval by its own rotation.

name: Alnair
description: A hot blue-white star and the brightest in the crane constellation Grus.

name: Alioth
description: The brightest star in the Big Dipper, with an unusual chemically peculiar spectrum.

name: Mirfak
description: A yellow supergiant that dominates the Perseus moving cluster.

name: Kaus Australis
description: The brightest star in Sagittarius, marking the base of the archer's bow.

name: Atria
description: An orange giant far more luminous than the Sun, brightest in the Southern Triangle.

name: Peacock
description: A hot blue-white binary and the only named star in the constellation Pavo.

name: Alphard
description: An orange giant whose name means 'the solitary one', isolated in a dim region of sky.

name: Hamal
description: An orange giant with a known exoplanet, once marking the vernal equinox.

name: Diphda
description: An orange giant brighter than Cetus's alpha star, with an unusually strong X-ray corona.

name: Alpheratz
description: A mercury-manganese star shared historically between Andromeda and Pegasus.

name: Rasalhague
description: A rapidly rotating white star at the head of the serpent-bearer.

name: Alphecca
description: The jewel of the Northern Crown, an eclipsing binary surrounded by a dust disk.

name: Eltanin
description: An orange giant that will pass close to the Sun in 1.5 million years.

name: Schedar
description: An orange giant marking the queen's breast in the W-shape of Cassiopeia.

name: Naos
description: One of the hottest and most luminous naked-eye stars, racing through space at high speed.

name: Ankaa
description: An orange giant binary and the brightest star of the Phoenix constellation.

name: Enif
description: An orange supergiant marking the nose of the winged horse, prone to sudden flares.

name: Alderamin
description: A fast-spinning white star that will become the pole star in about 5,500 years.

name: Sadalsuud
description: A yellow supergiant and the brightest star in Aquarius, whose name means luckiest of the lucky.

name: Beta Arae
description: An orange supergiant and the brightest star in Ara, over a hundred times the radius of the Sun.

name: Alpha Caeli
description: A white main-sequence star with a red dwarf companion, and the brightest star in the faint constellation Caelum.

name: Tarf
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Cancer, orbited by a confirmed giant planet.

name: Cor Caroli
description: The brightest star in Canes Venatici, a chemically peculiar star with one of the strongest magnetic fields known among main-sequence stars.

name: Deneb Algedi
description: An eclipsing binary and the brightest star in Capricornus, whose name means the tail of the goat.

name: Alpha Chamaeleontis
description: A white subgiant and the brightest star in the small southern constellation Chamaeleon.

name: Xami
description: The brightest star in Circinus and the brightest of the rapidly oscillating Ap stars, pulsating every seven minutes.

name: Phact
description: A blue-white star and the brightest in Columba, spinning fast enough to throw off a disc of gas.

name: Beta Comae Berenices
description: A close solar analogue and the brightest star in Coma Berenices, slightly larger and hotter than the Sun.

name: Gienah
description: A blue-white giant and the brightest star in Corvus, marking the wing of the crow.

name: Delta Crateris
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Crater, despite carrying a delta rather than an alpha designation.

name: Kitalpha
description: The brightest star in Equuleus, the second-smallest constellation, and a spectroscopic binary of a yellow giant and a white companion.

name: Dalim
description: A yellow-white subgiant with a white dwarf companion, and the brightest star in Fornax.

name: Kornephoros
description: A yellow giant and the brightest star in Hercules, its name meaning club-bearer.

name: Beta Hydri
description: The brightest star in Hydrus and one of the closest bright stars to the Sun, an older and more evolved version of it.

name: Alpha Indi
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Indus, sometimes called the Persian.

name: Stellio
description: A white main-sequence star and the brightest in Lacerta, a faint zigzag of stars between Cygnus and Andromeda.

name: Praecipua
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Leo Minor, whose name means the chief one.

name: Arneb
description: A yellow-white supergiant and the brightest star in Lepus, nearing the end of its life and likely to end as a supernova.

name: Zubeneschamali
description: The brightest star in Libra, once the northern claw of the scorpion, and often reported as looking faintly green.

name: Alpha Lyncis
description: A red giant and the brightest star in Lynx, a constellation said to need the eyes of a lynx to see.

name: Hoerikwaggo
description: A near twin of the Sun and the brightest star in Mensa, the faintest of all 88 constellations.

name: Alpha Muscae
description: A hot blue-white star and the brightest in Musca, pulsating slightly as a Beta Cephei variable.

name: Nu Octantis
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Octans, the constellation containing the south celestial pole.

name: Alpherg
description: A yellow giant and the brightest star in Pisces, a zodiac constellation with no star brighter than third magnitude.

name: Alpha Pyxidis
description: A hot blue giant and the brightest star in Pyxis, tens of thousands of times more luminous than the Sun.

name: Rhombus
description: A yellow giant and the brightest star in Reticulum, a small southern constellation named for a telescope eyepiece grid.

name: Alpha Sculptoris
description: A blue-white giant and the brightest star in Sculptor, the constellation containing the south galactic pole.

name: Tianbian
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Scutum, a small constellation set against a dense Milky Way star cloud.

name: Unukalhai
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Serpens, the only constellation split into two separate halves.

name: Alpha Sextantis
description: A white giant and the brightest star in Sextans, sitting almost exactly on the celestial equator.

name: Alpha Telescopii
description: A blue-white subgiant and the brightest star in Telescopium.

name: Lang-exster
description: An orange giant binary and the brightest star in Tucana, the constellation that hosts the Small Magellanic Cloud.

name: Alpha Antliae
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Antlia, suspected of varying slowly as it nears the end of its life.

name: Paradys
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Apus, some sixty times the radius of the Sun.

name: Beta Camelopardalis
description: A yellow supergiant and the brightest star in Camelopardalis, a large but famously dim northern constellation.

name: Meridiana
description: A white main-sequence star and the only named star in Corona Australis.

name: Alpha Doradus
description: A blue-white binary and the brightest star in Dorado, whose primary is a giant three and a half times the radius of the Sun.

name: Alpha Horologii
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Horologium, swollen to nearly ten times the diameter of the Sun.

name: Gamma Microscopii
description: A yellow giant and the brightest star in Microscopium, long since evolved off the main sequence.

name: Gamma2 Normae
description: An orange giant and the brightest star in Norma, a helium-fusing red clump star about ten times the radius of the Sun.

name: Alpha Pictoris
description: A fast-spinning white star and the brightest in Pictor, orbited by a companion every three and a half years.

name: Alaybasan
description: A white giant and the brightest star in Triangulum, locked in a 31-day orbit with a smaller companion.

name: Gamma2 Volantis
description: An orange giant and the brighter half of the wide double star that marks Volans.

name: Anser
description: A red giant and the brightest star in Vulpecula, forming a chance line-of-sight pair with the unrelated 8 Vulpeculae.

name: Pleiades
description: The brightest open cluster in the sky, a knot of hot blue stars that most people can pick out with the naked eye as six or seven points.

name: Hyades
description: The nearest open cluster to the Sun, forming the V-shaped face of Taurus, though Aldebaran only appears to belong to it and lies much closer.

name: Omega Centauri
description: The largest globular cluster in the galaxy, holding millions of stars, and possibly the stripped core of a galaxy the Milky Way swallowed.

name: Hercules Cluster (M13)
description: The finest globular cluster visible from northern latitudes, and the target of the 1974 Arecibo radio message.

name: Double Cluster
description: A pair of open clusters in Perseus that sit close enough together to share one telescope field, both only a few million years old.

name: 47 Tucanae
description: The second brightest globular cluster in the sky, dense enough at its core that its stars are separated by only a fraction of a light year.

name: GRB 221009A
description: The brightest gamma-ray burst ever recorded, so bright it saturated every detector pointed at it and disturbed Earth's ionosphere from two billion light years away.

name: SN 1987A
description: The nearest supernova seen since the invention of the telescope, and the first whose neutrinos were detected on Earth, three hours before the light arrived.
